Key

  1. Parcelle 4751 053 m²Bien-fonds, E-GRID CH380983458676. Zone d'habitation de faible densité, under the PEP “Vignoble de Corseaux” (1983).
  2. Emprise bâtie≈ 144–151 m²144 m² from the redrawn plans, 151 m² measured on the cadastre map. That is a COS of about 0.14.
  3. ≥ 6 m from limits≈ 388 m²PEP art. 10: extensions of existing buildings must stay 6 m from the neighbouring property line (8 m next to a vineyard). The hatched area is everything at least 6 m from all four sides. About 135 m² of it is already under the house.
  4. ↔ Current distances4.0 / 4.8 / 4.2 mTo parcels 476 (west), 477 (south-west) and 469 (east corner). The 1965 house is already closer than 6 m on these sides.
  5. Limite LRou art. 3618 mIndicative road building limit along the Chemin de Galatry. It crosses only the south corner of the parcel and stays well clear of the house.

Notes

How this was drawn

  • Traced over the scans from the Drive folder (“Plans étages” and “Plans de coupe et façades”). Positions follow the scans; they are not re-surveyed.
  • Figures on the drawings (levels, widths in cm) are copied from the originals.
  • Scale bars are approximate (about ±3 %) because the scans are photocopies of 1:50 sheets.

Differences from today

  • These are the 1963–64 drawings. Later works (roof redone 1998, west façade and windows 2008, kitchen and baths 1991) may have changed openings and fittings.
  • The listing describes 5 bedrooms and a studio kitchenette. The plan shows “bureau” and “studio” on the lower level, so room use has probably changed since.
  • Door swings and some small openings are hard to read on the scans and are simplified.

Before relying on it

  • For renovation budgeting or a permit file, have an architect or géomètre measure the house. A measured survey (relevé) typically replaces drawings like these.
  • The commune or the ECA may hold later permit drawings worth asking for.
